DISORDER\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr \/\u003E“\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EConversion disorder-Conversion disorder, also known as\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-family: UICTFontTextStyleEmphasizedItalicBody; font-style: italic;\"\u003Efunctional neurological symptom disorder (FND)\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E, is a psychiatric disorder characterized by symptoms affecting sensory or motor function. These signs and symptoms are inconsistent with patterns of known neurologic diseases or other medical conditions.”\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003EThe symptoms have \u003Cb\u003Eno organic basis\u003C\/b\u003E ,but cannot be controlled at will and are \u003Cb\u003Enot intentional\u003C\/b\u003E .\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003ECriteria to diagnose Conversion disorder (\u003Cb\u003EDSM 5)\u003C\/b\u003E- It categorises Conversion disorder as a part of -somatic symptoms and related disorders.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Col class=\"ol1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"li1\" style=\"font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EOne or more symptoms of altered voluntary motor or sensory function.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"li1\" style=\"font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EClinical findings can provide evidence of incompatibility between the symptom and recognized neurological or medical conditions.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"li1\" style=\"font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EAnother medical or mental disorder does not better explain the symptom or deficit.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"li1\" style=\"font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EThe symptom or deficit results in clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other vital areas of functioning or warrants medical evaluation.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ol\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK551567\/#:~:text=Conversion%20disorder%2C%20also%20known%20as,diseases%20or%20other%20medical%20conditions.\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK551567\/#:~:text=Conversion%20disorder%2C%20also%20known%20as,diseases%20or%20other%20medical%20conditions.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: UICTFontTextStyleBody;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMUNCHAUSEN SYNDROME \u003C\/b\u003E-\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003E“Munchausen syndrome, also called factitious disorder imposed on self, is a psychiatric disorder in which a person\u0026nbsp;assumes the role of a sick patient without the intention of external gain (time off from work, medications). Physical symptoms are \u003Cb\u003Eintentionally\u003C\/b\u003E produced with the purpose of gaining the appearance of a \"sick patient.\"”\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;It is not uncommon for the patient to purposefully induce symptoms, such as intentionally eating spoiled food, injecting insulin, picking at skin causing wounds, overdosing on medications, and not taking medications as prescribed. In addition, patients have been known to forge medical records and tamper with laboratory results.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDiagnosis with DSM 5\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003EThis criterion includes evidence that the patient is taking steps to \u003Cb\u003Eintentionally\u003C\/b\u003E and \u003Cb\u003Efalsely\u003C\/b\u003E represent a psychiatric or general medical condition without evidence of malingering, and the behavior is independent of other medical or psychiatric conditions, such as schizophrenia and delusional disorder\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK518999\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK518999\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ELEARNING POINTS FROM CASE DISCUSSION\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003E1. font-size: 12pt;\"\u003EThe patient was apparently asymptomatic 1 year ago , when she developed an abscess in the posterior aspect of her right thigh , that was insidious onset , progressive ( initially being about 1cm , progressing to about 3-4 inches ), with redness and hardening of the surrounding skin and local rise of temperature over the swelling .It was associated with pain ,insidious in onset, that was dragging type in character , progressive , non radiating , with no aggravating factors , but relieved on taking medications .Also associated with low grade fever, without chills and rigors, that lasted for 4-6 days after the abscess appeared .\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"line-height: normal; margin-bottom: 0cm;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: Times, serif;\"\u003E10 days later -Due to the swelling progressing in size ,the patient went to the doctor .Incision and drainage of the pus was performed . The patient was prescribed antibiotics and ointment , that the patient used for 1 month .Following the hospital visit the patient’s husband would drain the abscess twice a day for 15 days at home.The abscess healed after a month and the patient complains of the area being hard since then .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"line-height: normal; margin-bottom: 0cm;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: Times, serif;\"\u003EDuring the course of treatment, the patient's family started noticing a reduction in her weight. Over a period of 1 year, the patient lost at least 12kg of weight, from 75 kgs initially to 63 kgs. Not \u0026nbsp;associated with decreased appetite . The patient has been unable to gain any weight even after trying to gain weight .The patient complains of loss of lustre of the skin and dryness ,and having a dull appearance .\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"line-height: normal; margin-bottom: 0cm;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: Times, serif;\"\u003EThe patient also complains of hair fall and dryness of hair ,since 1 year that reduced on taking medication ( multivitamins and iron supplements ).\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"line-height: normal; margin-bottom: 0cm;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: Times, serif;\"\u003EThe patient also complains of irregular menstrual cycles since 1 year .\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"line-height: normal; margin-bottom: 0cm;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: Times, serif;\"\u003EThe patient also complains of dark spots and redness on face ,that aggravates on exposure to sun and have become more prominent since 1 year .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"line-height: normal;
